basis: Fibrocystic changes are confined to breast tissue, which has no axis.
Immune-mediated granulomatous inflammation of the cerebrum; damaging extracranial involvement is not established for this concept.
Hereditary motor neuron/peripheral nerve disease; weakness reflects denervation rather than primary muscle disease.
Carcinoma of the abdominal peritoneal lining, assigned to the gastrointestinal axis; additional organ invasion is not universal.
Primary neoplasm arising in the heart; embolic injury elsewhere is not consistently present.
Unilateral developmental deformity of the distal radius and wrist.
Congenital structural myopathy; global developmental delay is annotated in 80-99%, supporting neurologic involvement, although motor impairment may contribute.
Hypertrophy and folding of scalp skin; neurologic, ocular and hearing abnormalities characterize only some subtypes.
Adrenal steroid synthesis disorder defined by hormone deficiencies and hypokalemic hypertension; hypertension occurs in 80-99%.
Warburg micro syndrome combines severe neurodevelopmental impairment, congenital cataracts/microphthalmia and characteristic hypogonadism.
Chronic purulent infection and inflammation within the eye.
Neoplasm originating in the uterine corpus; reproductive organs have no axis.
Impaired cerebral integration of visual forms; this is a higher visual processing disorder rather than intrinsic eye damage.
Inherited myxomatous mitral valve disease with prolapse and regurgitation.
Defining skeletal and nail dysplasia; intrinsic nephropathy affects ~30-50%. Iris pigmentation is non-damaging; glaucoma is a minority risk.
Inherited platelet procoagulant dysfunction; mucosal bleeding and bruising do not establish separate organ damage.
Obstetric umbrella concept; no listed organ is consistently affected across pregnancy, childbirth and puerperal disorders.
Skeletal dysplasia; hearing impairment in 6/9 and intellectual disability in 10/30 support involvement. Absent frontal sinuses alone do not establish airway dysfunction.
Pelvic reproductive endometriosis; bowel, urinary tract or other listed organ infiltration is not specified.
Tetrahydrobiopterin metabolism defect causing central neurotransmitter deficiency and dystonia; oculogyric crises reflect neurologic dysfunction.
Usually viral or bacterial inflammation of the pharynx, included in the upper airway axis.
Inherited platelet dysfunction with macrothrombocytopenia and bleeding; bleeding sites do not indicate intrinsic organ disease.
Syrinx formation damages the spinal cord; scoliosis frequency is unspecified, and urinary symptoms can reflect neurologic dysfunction.
Benign neoplasm arising in the adrenal gland; hormone excess and secondary organ injury are not universal across subtypes.
Neurodevelopmental disorder; elevated LDL in 2/2 supports lipid metabolic involvement, and developmental cataract occurs in 1/3. Frequency estimates use very small cohorts.
